Empirical Research Plan: Bank-competition Shocks and State-Level Innovation, 1976–2006  

=====================================================================  

1. Identification Strategy  
----------------------------------  
• Method: Staggered Difference-in-Differences (event-study implementation).  
• Rationale:  
  – The four IBBEA provisions were relaxed at different calendar years across states, generating plausibly exogenous, discrete shifts in bank-entry barriers (Rice & Strahan 2010).  
  – We observe annual outcomes for each state (aggregated for public and private firms) for two decades before and after the first wave of deregulation; thus we can compare within-state changes in innovation around removal of restrictions to contemporaneous changes in states that have not (yet) deregulated.  
  – Because adoption is staggered, we will use the Callaway & Sant’Anna (2021) group-time average treatment effect estimator (and Sun & Abraham 2020 event-time coefficients) to avoid bias from differential timing.  
  – For channel tests we add a third (or fourth) difference: e.g., finance dependence × listed/private × deregulation.  

2. Treatment and Control  
----------------------------------  
Treatment variable  
  – Primary: Dereg_i,t = 1 if in calendar year t state i has removed ALL four interstate branching barriers; 0 otherwise.  
  – Intensity (robustness): DeregIndex_i,t = 4 – (# of remaining restrictions), ranges 0–4.  

Control group  
  – States that have not yet fully deregulated in year t.  
  – After their own adoption they exit the control pool (absorbing treatment).  

Treatment timing  
  – TreatYear_i = first year in which Dereg_i,t switches from 0 to 1.  
  – Event time k = t – TreatYear_i (−10 … +10 in estimation window).  

Unit of observation  
  – Baseline: state-year for innovation aggregates.  
  – Extensions: corporation-year or private-firm-year with firm fixed effects.  

3. Key Identifying Assumptions  
----------------------------------  
A1. Parallel trends: Absent deregulation, innovation outcomes in treated states would have evolved like those in not-yet-treated states. Plausibility: IBBEA’s timing was driven by politics and bank-lobby bargaining rather than state-specific innovation trajectories; we will check with pre-trend event-study plots.  

A2. No anticipation: Firms did not significantly adjust innovative activity before the legal change. Plausible because exact relaxation dates and details were difficult to predict; we will test for pre-effects (k = −5 … −1).  

A3. SUTVA / no cross-state spillovers: Innovation in one state is not directly affected by another state’s deregulation. Plausibility moderate—mobile inventors or M&A flows could transmit shocks. We address with (i) excluding border-share patenters, (ii) spatial lags robustness.  

A4. Stable composition: The set of headquarters does not differentially migrate because of deregulation in anticipation windows. Will verify by tracking headquarters moves.  

4. Main Threats and Mitigations  
----------------------------------  
Threat 1: Differential pre-trends or coincident state policies (e.g., R&D tax credits).  
  • Mitigation: event-study graphs; include state-specific linear or industry-specific trends; control for R&D tax credits and state macro controls.  

Threat 2: Spillovers across neighboring states (bank branches or inventor migration).  
  • Mitigation: drop border-counties, or include neighbor-state deregulation indicator; perform border-pair matched DID where each treated state is compared only with contiguous states not yet treated.  

Threat 3: Endogenous headquarters relocation.  
  • Mitigation: (i) treat the HQ move itself as an outcome; (ii) keep firm fixed effects and allocate patents by HQ at application year; (iii) replicate using inventors’ state of residence (NBER disambiguated inventors) to anchor innovation geographically independent of corporate HQ.  

5. R Code Outline  
----------------------------------  
```r
############################################################
# 0. Packages
############################################################
library(data.table)
library(fixest)       # fast high-dim FE regressions
library(did)          # Callaway & Sant’Anna
library(ggplot2)

############################################################
# 1. Load data  (assume csv files in ./data)
############################################################
state_year <- fread("./data/state_year_panel.csv")   # outcomes + controls
dereg       <- fread("./data/ibbea_restrictions.csv") # 4 provisions, by state-year

############################################################
# 2. Construct treatment variables
############################################################
# DeregIndex: # removed restrictions
dereg[, DeregIndex := 4 - (age_req + denovo + branch_acq + dep_cap)]  # each var 0/1
dereg[, Dereg := fifelse(DeregIndex==4, 1L, 0L)]

# Merge with panel
panel <- merge(state_year, dereg[, .(state, year, Dereg, DeregIndex)], 
               by = c("state","year"), all.x = TRUE)

# First-treatment year per state
panel[, treat_year := ifelse(any(Dereg==1), min(year[Dereg==1]), NA), by = state]

############################################################
# 3. Callaway-Sant’Anna DID (state-year outcome: log patents)
############################################################
cs_res <- att_gt(yname = "log_pat_pubcorp",  # public corp patents
                 tname = "year",
                 idname = "state",
                 gname = "treat_year",          # group = first treatment year
                 xformla = ~ gsp + ind_emp_share1:ind_emp_share8,
                 data = panel)

event_res <- aggte(cs_res, type = "dynamic")  # event-study ATT

# Plot pre-trend diagnostics
ggplot(data = data.frame(event_res$egt, event_res$att, event_res$se), 
       aes(x = event_res.egt, y = event_res.att)) +
  geom_point() + geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = att - 1.96*se, ymax = att + 1.96*se)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = -0.5, lty = 2) + theme_minimal() +
  labs(x = "Event time (years)", y = "ATT on log patents")

############################################################
# 4. Main two-way FE spec with fixest (corporation-year level)
############################################################
firmyear <- fread("./data/firm_year_panel.csv")
# Merge treatment by HQ state-year
firmyear <- merge(firmyear, panel[, .(state, year, Dereg)], 
                  by = c("state","year"), all.x = TRUE)

# Baseline: log(1+patents) as DV
reg1 <- feols(lpatents ~ Dereg + size + roa + leverage + i(year) | gvkey + state^year, 
              data = firmyear, cluster = "state")
summary(reg1)

############################################################
# 5. Robustness: border-pair matched DID
############################################################
# Pre-made file border_pairs with {state, border_state}
bp <- fread("./data/border_pairs.csv")
firmyear_bp <- merge(firmyear, bp, by = "state")
reg_border <- feols(lpatents ~ Dereg | gvkey + i(year, border_state),
                    data = firmyear_bp, cluster = "state")
summary(reg_border)
```

6. Expected Results  
----------------------------------  
Theory predicts that lower entry barriers increase bank competition → cheaper/more plentiful credit, especially for opaque, external-finance-dependent firms. Innovation (patent counts, citations) should rise.  
• Public corporations: +5% to +8% in annual patent counts, larger (+10%–15%) in citations.  
• Private firms: larger semi-elasticities (+10%–12%) because they rely more on bank debt.  
• Channels: strongest effects for industries in the top quartile of external-finance dependence; larger when pre-IBBEA lender concentration was high; incremental patents disproportionately cross-classified in generality/originality (i.e., higher quality).  

7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (DID)  
----------------------------------  
C1: Parallel pre-trends visually and statistically verified ………………… 1  
C2: No anticipation (flat coefficients k = −5 … −1) ………………………… 1  
C3: No time-varying confounders (controls + trends) …………………… 0.5  
C4: No interference across units (spillovers limited) …………………… 0.5  
C5: Proper estimator for staggered timing (CS / SA) …………………….. 1  
TOTAL = 4/5 → overall credible but spillovers and concurrent policies remain caveats.
